FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Soil Quality 
and Fertilizers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 


Composts are excellent source of organic carbon and are the basic food material for all the microorganisms present 
in the soil, but are very poor in terms of fertilizing nutrients. Keeping in view of their growing requirement for 
sustenance of soil health and fertility, need is also being felt to enrich them nutritionally through natural sources 
of nutrients. Nutritionally rich composts/manures will not only provide much needed organic matter for required 
biological activity, but will also help in reducing the requirements of nutrients in chemical form. Nutrients applied 
through the route of composts have an additional advantage of theirhigher use efficiency. 


Phosphate rich organic manure (PROM) is nutrient rich compost, obtained by the co-composting of organic 
matter, including municipal solid waste with rock phosphate as natural phosphorus source. During the microbial 
degradation process, part of the insoluble phosphorus present in the rock phosphate gets converted into available 
form through the activity of microorganisms and is available to plants immediately after its application. 
Application of naturally occurring phosphate along with compost can be an ideal fertilizer Phosphate replacement 
in due course of time. 


Use of farm yard manure or agro-waste in conjunction with rock phosphate is the ideal choice for PROM making, 
but use of municipal solid waste compost requires some degree of precaution to avoid the incorporation of heavy 
metals. This Indian Standard for PROM has been prepared with the aim to ensure consistent quality of PROM 
with adequate quantity of phosphorus in the available form along with the total phosphorus strength. This standard 
also provides for maximum acceptable concentrations of heavy metals to ensure that consistent usage of such 
inputs over a long period of time does not pose any health hazard to soil and crop productivity. 


With the growing awareness for maintenance of soil health and fertility, demand is growing for organicfertilizers. 
Ensuring the availability of phosphorus through organic way is a recent phenomenon and is being promoted as 
ideal phosphorus source with high degree of use efficiency. Many industries and trading house have started 
producing and trading the PROM. To ensure the quality to the farmers and to maintain the standards during 
production process for manufacturers, standards and its testing procedures are needed. 


Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex L. 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the Fertilizer (Control) Order, 1985 
and Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 of Government of India. However, this standard is 
subject to restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision), The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard 
PHOSPHATE RICH ORGANIC MANURE — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements, methods 
of sampling and tests for phosphate rich organic 
manure. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following Indian Standards contain provisions 
which through reference in this text constitutes 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent edition of the standard listed below:

IS 460 (Part 1) Test sieves — Specification: 
: 2020 Part 1 Wire cloth test sieves 
(fourth revision) 


IS 1070: 1992 Reagent grade water (third 
revision) 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1 Compost — Substance made of one or more 
unprocessed waste material of biological nature 
(plant and animal) and may include unprocessed 


mineral material that has been altered through 
microbiological decomposition. 


3.2 Municipal Solid Waste Compost (MSWC) — 
Product made from biodegradable municipal solid 
waste which has been altered into manure through 
microbiological decomposition. 


3.3 Phosphate Rich Organic Manure (PROM) — 
Substance made of one or more unprocessed waste 
material of biological nature (plant and animal) and 
unprocessed mineral rock phosphate that has been 
altered through microbiological decomposition. 


3.4 Rock Phosphate — Rock phosphate is a mined 
sedimentary rock which contains high amounts of 
phosphate bearing mineral in highly insoluble form. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 
4.1 Description 


The PROM shall be in powdered or granular form, 
dark brown to black in colour with no foul odour. 


4.2 Particle Size 


The particle size of PROM shall not be more than 
6.0 mm, and a minimum of 90 percent of PROM 
shall pass through 6.0 mm IS sieve 
[see IS 460 (Part 1)]. 


4.3 The product shall also conform to the 
requirements given in Table 1.

5 PACKING, MARKING AND STORAGE 
5.1 Packing 


PROM shall be packed in the manner as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the supplier. Each bag 
shall be securely closed. 


5.2 Marking 


5.2.1 Each pack shall be marked legibly and 
indelibly with the following information: 


a) Name and type of the material; 

b) Name, address of the manufacturer; 

c) Indication of the source of manufacture; 

d) Percent by mass of total phosphorous to 
total dry mass; 

e) Percent by mass of total 
phosphorus to total dry mass; 

f) C:Nratio; 

g) Gross and net quantity in kg; 

h) Batch number, in code or otherwise, to 
enable the lot of manufacture to be traced 
back from records; and 

j) Any other information as required under 
Fertilizer (Control) Order, 1985 and the 
Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


available 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


6 SAMPLING 
6.1 General Requirements of Sampling 


In drawing samples, the following measures and 


precautions should be observed: 


a) Samples shall not be taken at a place exposed 

to rain/sun. 

The sampling instruments shall be clean and 

dry when used. 

c) The material being sampled, the sampling 
instruments and the bags of samples shall be 
free from any adventitious contaminations. 

d) To draw a representative sample, the 
contents of each bag selected for sampling 
shall be mixed as thoroughly as possible by 
suitable means. 
The sample shall be kept in a suitable, clean, 
dry and airtight glass or screwed hard 
polythene bottle of about 400 g capacity or 
in a thick-gauged polyethylene bag. This 
shall be put in a cloth bag, which shall be 
sealed after putting inside the detailed 
description. 

f) Identifiable details may also be put on the 

cloth bag like sample no./code no. or any 

other details which enables its identification. 

Each sample bag shall be sealed air tight 

after filling and marked with details of 

sample.

6.2 Sampling from Bagged Material 
6.2.1 Scale of Sampling 
6.2.1.1 Lot (for manufacturers) 


All bags in a single consignment of the material of 
the same total organic carbon, nitrogen, 
phosphorous and potassium content and С: N ratio 
derived from the same source of manufacture drawn 
from a single batch of the manufacturer shall 
constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared to 
consist of different batches of manufacturer, all the 
bags of each batch shall constitute a separate lot. In 
the case of a consignment drawn from a continuous 
process, 2 000 bags (or 100 tonnes) of the material 


shall constitute a lot. 
6.2.1.2 Lot (for dealer) 


The lot is an identifiable quantity of manure with 
same total organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorous 
and potassium content and C : N ratio derived from 
the same source of manufacture stored at an 
identifiable place subject to a maximum limit of 100 
tones. The lot shall be identified based on visible 
appearance of bags, their packing and storage 
conditions. The stock of less than 100 tones with a 
dealer may alsoconstitute one or more lots, if the 
material of different sources and brand is available 
in such quantities. 


6.2.1.3 Selection of bags for sampling 


The number of bags to be chosen from a lot shall be 
in accordance with Table 2. 


Table 2 Number of Containers to be Selected for 


Sampling 
(Clause 6.2)

All the bags of a lot should be arranged in a 
systematic manner. Start counting from any bag 
randomly; go on counting as 1,2,3,....up to R and so 
on. R being equal to the integral of N/n. Thus, every 
4" bag counted shall be withdrawn and all bags 
shall constitute the sample bags from where the 
sample is to be drawn for preparing a composite 
sample. 


6.3 Sampling from Big Godowns/High Stockings 


If the procedure given in 6.2.1.3 is not possible to be 
adopted, the sample should be drawn from the 
randomly selected compost bags from different 
layers, from top and from all open sides in a zig-zag 
fashion. 


6.3.1 Sampling from Small Godowns 


All the fertilizer bags of the same grade and type of 
each manufacturer though received on different 


IS 18146 : 2023 


dates shallbe segregated and properly stacked. All 
bags of same grade and type of compost 
manufactured by a particular manufacturing unit 
may be considered as one lot based on their physical 
conditions and the sample shall be drawn as per 
procedure laid down in 6.2.1.3 and 6.4. 


6.4 Sampling Probe 


6.4.1 An appropriate sampling instrument to be used 
for collection of a representative sample is called 
sampling probe. The probe may comprise of a 
slotted single tube with solid cone tip made of 
stainless steel or brass. The length of the probe may 
be approximately 60 cm to 65 cm and the diameter 
of the tube may be approximately 1.5 cm and the slot 
width may be 1.2 cm to 1.3 cm. The probe may be 
used if the physical condition of the manure and the 
packing material permits its use. 


6.4.2 In case of high-density polythene packing and 
also when the manure is not in free flowing 
condition, the use of sampling probe may not be 
possible. In such case, selected bags for drawing 
samples may be opened and the fertilizers may be 
taken out of the bags and spread on a clean surface 
and samples drawn with the help of a suitable 
sampling device, which may be made of stainless 
steel or brass cup. 


6.5 Drawal of Samples from Bags 


6.5.1 Drawal of Sample and Preparation of 
Composite Samples 


Draw, with an appropriate sampling instrument, 
(sampling probe) small portions of the material 
from the selected bags as per procedure in 6.2.1.2 
and 6.2.1.3. The sampling probe shall be inserted in 
the bag from one corner to another diagonally and 
when filled with fertilizer, the probe is withdrawn 
and fertilizer is emptied in a container/ or on 
polythene sheet/or on a clean hard surface and 
made into one composite sample. 


6.5.2 If the bags do not permit the use of sampling 
probe, empty the contents of the bags on a level, 
clean and hard surface and draw a composite 
sample by the process of quartering as described 
under 6.7. 


6.6 Quantity of One Sample 


One sample of PROM shall have approximately 
500 g. 


6.7 Preparation of Composite Sample 


If the composite sample collected from the different 
selected bags is larger than required quantity, its 
size shall be reduced by method of quartering. For 
quartering, spread the composite sample on a level, 


IS 18146 : 2023 


clean, hard surface, flatten it out and divide it into 
four equal parts. Remove any diagonally opposite 
parts. Mix the two remaining parts together to form 
a cone, flatten out the cone and repeat the operation 
of quartering till a composite sample of required 
quantity is obtained. 


6.8 Preparation of Test Sample and Reference 
Sample 


6.8.1 The composite sample obtained above shall be 
spread out on a clean, hard surface and divided into 
three approximately equal portions each of the 
weight as specified in 6.6. Each of these samples 
shall constitute the test sample. 


6.8.2 Each test sample shall be immediately 
transferred to a suitable container as defined under 


6.1 e). The slip with detailed description may be 
put inside the sample bag. Each bag shall also be 
properly labeled as mentioned in 5.2. 


6.8.3 Each test sample container shall then be sealed. 
7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods 
prescribed in 4. 


7.2 Unless otherwise specified, quality reagents, 
chemicals and distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be 
employedin tests. 


NOTE — 'Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect experimental results.

ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SINO. (i)] 


ESTIMATION OF BULK DENSITY 


A-1 APPARATUS 


Weighing balance, measuring cylinder (100 ml), 
rubber pad (0.093 m?; 2.57 cm thickness), hot air 
oven. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


Dry the PROM sample in a hot air oven at 60 *C for 
24 hours. Weigh a dry 100 ml cylinder. Fill the 
cylinder withthe sample up to the 100 ml mark. 
Weigh the cylinder along with the sample. Tap the 
cylinder for two min for compacting the sample. 
Measure the compact volume. 


A-3 CALCULATION 


W.-— W 
Bulk density, (g/cm?) = 2 tt 


where 


W, = Mass, in g, of the dry 100 ml cylinder 
W, = Mass, in g, of the dry 100 ml cylinder 
with sample 
V = Final volume, in ml, upto which the 
sample is present in the 
cylinder after compaction 


ANNEXB 
[Table 1, SI No. (11)] 


ESTIMATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT 


B-1 APPARATUS 


Petri dish, hot air oven, desiccator, weighing 
balance. 


B-2 PROCEDURE 


Weigh a clean dry petri dish. Take approximately 
(weigh to the nearest mg) 10 g of the prepared 
sample in the petri dish. Heat in an oven for about 
24 hours at 70 *C to constant weight. Cool in a 
desiccator and weigh. Report percentage loss in 
weight as moisture content. 


B-3 CALCULATION 


А 100 (В – С) 
Moisture percent by mass = NTE 


where 


A = Mass, in g, of the petri dish 

B = Mass, in g, of the petri dish with sample, 
before drying 

C = Mass, in g, of the petri dish with sample, 
after drying 


ANNEX C 
[Table 1, SI No. (111)] 


ESTIMATION OF pH 


C-1 REAGENT — Distilled water 


C-2 APPARATUS — Rotary shaker, Whatman no. 
1 or equivalent filter paper, Buchner funnel fitted 
with vacuum pump, pH meter. 


C-3 PROCEDURE 


Make 25 g of PROM into a suspension in 50 ml of 


distilled water and shake on a rotary shaker for 
2 hours. Filter through Whatman no. 1 or 
equivalent filter paper under vacuum using a 
Buchner funnel. Determine pH of the filtrate by 
pH meter. 


IS 18146 : 2023 


ANNEX D 
[Table 1, 81 No. (iv)] 


ESTIMATION OF CONDUCTIVITY 


D-1 REAGENTS — Potassium chloride (AR 
grade), distilled water. 


D-2 APPARATUS — Conductivity meter (with 
temperature compensation system), 4 mm sieve, 
flask (250 ml), funnel (outer diameter = 75 mm), 
beaker (100 ml), analytical balance, filter paper. 


D-3 PROCEDURE 
Pass fresh sample of PROM through a 4 mm sieve. 


Take 20 g of the sample and add 100 ml of distilled 
water to it to give a ratio of 1:5. Stir for an hour at 
regular intervals. Calibrate the conductivity meter 
by using 0.01 M potassium chloride solution. 
Measure the conductivity of the unfiltered compost 
suspension. Express the results as dsm! at 25 °C 
specifying the dilution of the compost suspension, 
that is, 1:5. 


ANNEX E 
[Table 1, 81 No. (v)] 


ESTIMATION OF TOTAL ORGANIC CARBON 


E-1 APPARATUS 


Silica/platinum crucible (60 ml capacity), muffle 
furnace, analytical balance, hot air oven, desiccator. 


E-2 PROCEDURE 


Accurately weigh 10 g oven dried sample (70 °C 
for 24 hours) in to a pre-weighed crucible and 
ignite thematerial in a muffle furnace at 550 °C for 
4 hours. Cool to room temperature and keep in 
desiccator for 12 hours. Weigh the contents with 
crucible. 


E-3 CALCULATION 


Calculate the total organic carbon by the following 
formulae:

mass)

ANNEX F 
[Table 1, 81 Мо. (vi) and (vii)] 
ESTIMATION OF TOTAL PHOSPHOROUS AND TOTAL CITRATE SOLUBLE PHOSPHORUS 


F-1 PREPARATION OF SAMPLE FOR 
ESTIMATION OF TOTAL PHOSPHORUS 


F-1.1 Reagent 


Concentrated nitric acid, 70 percent to 72 percent 
perchloric acid, distilled water 


F-1.2 Apparatus 


Conical flasks, kjeldahl long neck flasks (500 ml 
capacity), beaker (100 ml), Whatman no.1 filter 
paper, hotplate, volumetric flask (100 ml) 


F-1.3 Procedure 


Accurately weigh 1 g oven dried sample (at 70 °C 
for 24 hours) in a long neck Kjeldahl digestion flask; 
add 20 ml to 30 ml concentrated nitric acid and boil 
gently for 30 min to 45 min. Cool and add 10 ml to 
20 ml of 70 percent to 72 percent perchloric acid. 
Boil gently till fuming point until solution is 
colorless or nearly so for about an hour. Do not boil 
to dryness at any time. Cool slightly and add 50 ml 
water and boil for few min. Cool and filter. 
Transfer the filtrate to 100 ml volumetric flask and 
make up the volume to 100 ml. 


F-2 PREPARATION OF SAMPLE FOR 
ESTIMATION OF TOTAL CITRATE 
SOLUBLE PHOSPHORUS 


F-2.1 Reagent 
F-2.1.1 Ammonium Citrate Solution 


Dissolve 300 g pure citric acid in 1 500 ml distilled 
water. Add approximately 345 ml of 28 percent to 
29 percent of ammonium hydroxide so than acid is 
neutralized and a pH of 7.0 is attained. pH can be 
adjusted by adding ammonium hydroxide or citric 
acid solutions. This can be stored up to 6 months. 
Frequently check pH, if changed make it neutral. 


F-2.2 Apparatus 


Conical flasks, volumetric flasks, water bath, 
Buchner funnel, vacuum pump. 


F- 2.3 Procedure 


F-2.3.1 Take 1 g of accurately weighed oven dried 
sample in a conical flask and add 100 ml of neutral 
ammonium citrate solution previously heated to 
65 °C over water bath. 


F-2.3.2 Stopper the flask with rubber cork and 
shake vigorously for 10 min. Release pressure by 
opening cork occasionally. 


F-2.3.3 Heat the flask on water bath at 65 °C for 
about an hour. 


F-2.3.4 Filter the contents using filter pump/vacuum 
pump (through Whatman no. 5 filter paper or 
Buchner funnel) and wash with about 50 ml of 
distilled water. Transfer the filtrate to 200 ml 
volumetric flask and make up the volume to 200 ml. 


F-2.3.5 Take suitable aliquot of this extract and 
estimate P by gravimetric method as described 
below. 


F-3 GRAVIMETRIC QUINOLINE METHOD 
FOR DETERMINATION OF TOTAL 
PHOSPHORUS 


F-3.1 Reagents 


F-3.1.1 Citric Molybdic Acid Reagent 


Dissolve 54 g, 100 percent molybdic anhydride 
(MoO;) and 12 g NaOH with stirring in 400 ml hot 
water and cool. Dissolve 60 g citric acid in mixture 
of 140 ml HCl and 300 ml water and cool. Gradually 
add molybdic solution to citric acid solution with 
stirring. Cool, filter and dilute to 1 litre (solution 
may be green or blue colour depending on exposure 
to light). If necessary, add 0.5 percent KBrO; 
solution drop by drop until green colour becomes 
pale. Store in dark in polyethylene bottle. 


F-3.1.2 Quinoline Solution 


Dissolve 50 ml synthetic quinoline with stirring in 
mixture of 60 ml HCI and 300 ml water. Cool dilute 
to | litre and filter. Store in polyethylene bottle. 


F-3.1.3 Quimociac Reagent 


Dissolve 70 g of sodium molybdate dehydrate in 
150 ml water. Dissolve 60 g citric acid in mixture 
of 85 ml HNO; and 150 ml water and cool. 
Gradually add molybdate solution to citric acid- 
nitric acid mixture with stirring. Dissolve 5 ml 
synthetic quinoline in mixture of 35 ml HNO, and 
100 ml water. Gradually add this solution to 
molybdate-citric-nitric acid solution mix and let it 
stand for 24 hours. Filter, add 280 ml acetone, dilute 
to 1 litre with water and mix well. Store in 
polyethylene bottle. 


IS 18146 : 2023 


F-3.2 Apparatus 


Erlenmeyer flask, pipette, watch glass, hot plate, 
sintered glass gooch crucible Grade 4 (30 ml 
capacity), desiccators. 


F-3.3 Procedure 


In 500 ml Erlenmeyer flask, pipette aliquot 
containing not more than 25 mg Р,О; (as prepared 
above by the methods described at F-1 and F-2), 
dilute to approximately 100 ml with water. Proceed 
with one of the following method. 


F-3.3.1 Add 30 ml citric-molybdic acid reagent and 
boil gently for 3 min (solution must be precipitate 
free at this stage). Remove from heat and swirl 
carefully. Immediately add from burette 10 ml 
quinoline solution with continuous swirling (add 
first 3 ml to 4 ml drop wise and remainder in steady 
stream). 


F-3.3.2 Add 50 ml quimociac reagent, cover with 
watch glass place on hot plate in well ventilated 
hood and boil for 1 min. 


After treatment with F-3.3.1 or F-3.3.2, cool to room 
temperature, swirl carefully 3-4 times during 
cooling, filterthrough sintered glass Gooch crucible 
Grade 4 (30 ml capacity), previously dried at 250 °C 
and weighed, and wash 5 times with 25 ml portion 
of water. Dry the crucible and contents for 30 min at 
250 °C. Cool in desiccator to constant weight as 
quinoline phosphomolybdate [(C,H,;N)3H3;PO, 
.12MoO;]. Estimate blank reading withoutsample. 
Subtract blank weight. Multiply by 0.032 O7 to 
obtain weight of P,O;. Report as percent Р„О;. 


F-3.4 Calculation 


Total phosphorus (as P,O,;), percent by mass of total 
dry mass: 


= (A -B) x 0.032 07 


where 


A = Mass, in g, of quinoline phosphomolybdate 


obtained by treatment of sample ; and 
B = Mass, in g, of quinoline phosphomolybdate 
in blank treatment. 


ANNEX G 
[Table 1, SI No. (viii)] 


CALCULATION OF С : N RATIO 


G-1 PROCEDURE 


The C : N ratio is calculated using total organic 
carbon, percent by mass of total dry mass 
determined at E-3 and total nitrogen (as N), percent 
by mass of total dry mass determined at G-2.4. 


G-1.1 CALCULATION 
C:Nratio=A:B 
where 


A = total organic carbon, percent by mass of 
total dry mass determined at E-3; and 


B = total nitrogen (as N), percent by mass of 
total dry mass determined at G-2.4 


G-2 ESTIMATION OF TOTAL NITROGEN 
G-2.1 Apparatus 


G-2.1.1 Suitable Kjeldahl assembly consisting of 
500 ml to 800 ml round bottom, digestion flask and 
kjeldahl distillation assembly consisting of 500 ml 


to 800 ml distillation flask, splash head tube and 
condenser, all with appropriate glass joints. The 
length of the condenser's delivery tube should be 
long enough to keep immersed in a flask for 
ammonia absorption. 


G-2.1.2 Kjeldahl digestion unit with heating control, 
suitable for 500 ml to 800 ml flasks. 


G-2.2 REAGENTS 
G-2.2.1 Sulphuric Acid, 93-98 Percent, N-free. 
G-2.2.2 Salicylic Acid, reagent grade, N-free. 


G-2.2.3 Sodium Thiosulphate (Na,S,0;-5H,O), 
reagent grade. 


G-2.2.4 Zinc Dust, Impalpable Powder. 
G-2.2.5 Copper Sulphate 


G-2.2.6 Potassium or Sodium Sulphate 
G-2.2.7 45 percent NaOH Solution 
Dissolve 450 gm of Sodium hydroxide pellets in 


distilled water and makeup the volume to 1 000 ml. 
G-2.2.8 Methyl Red Indicator 
Dissolve 1 gm methyl red in 200 ml alcohol. 


G-2.2.9 Hydrochloric or Sulphuric Acid Standard 
Solution, 0.1 N or as per requirement. 


G-2.2.10 Sodium Hydroxide Standard Solution, 
0.1 N or as per Requirement. 


G-2.3 PROCEDURE 


Place weighed sample (0.7 g to 2.2 g) in digestion 
flask. Add 40 ml H,SO, containing 2 g salicylic 
acid. Shake until thoroughly mixed and let stand, 
with occasional shaking, 30 min or more. Then add 
5 g Na)S,03.5H,O or 2 g zinc dust (as impalpable 
powder not granulated zinc or filing). Shake the 
flask and let it stand for five min then heat over low 
flame until frothing ceases. 


Turn off heat, add 0.7 g copper sulphate, 15 g 
powdered K,SO, (or anhydrous Na,SO,) and boil 
briskly until solution clears, continue boiling for 
another at least 2 hour. Remove from burner and 
cool, add 200 ml of water and swirl the flask to 
dissolve all the contents. Transfer to 500 ml 
volumetric flask, giving several washings with 
water to the digestion flask. Make up the volume to 


500 ml. 
Take 25 ml aliquot in the distillation flask; add 


300 ml water and a pinch of zinc dust. Take 20 ml 
of standard acid solution in the receiving conical 
flask, add 4 drops of methyl red indicator and keep 
the flask at the lower end of the condenser in such a 
way that the lower tip of the condenser is fully 
immersed in acid solution. 


IS 18146 : 2023 


Add 30 ml of 45 percent NaOH to the distillation 
flask, gently so that the contents do not mix. 
Immediately connect the flask to distillation 
assembly and swirl to mix the contents. Heat until 
all the ammonia is distilled (at least 150 ml 
distillate). Remove from receiving flask. Rinse 
outlet tube into receiving flask with a small amount 
of distilled water. 


Titrate the contents in the receiver conical flask 
with standard NaOH solution. Determine blank on 
reagents using same quantity of standard acid in 
receiving conical flask. 


G-2.4 CALCULATION 


Total nitrogen (as N), percent by mass of total dry 
mass 


WwW 


where 


Vı = Volume, in ml, of standard acid taken in 

receiver flask for sample; 

V2 = Volume, in ml, of standard NaOH used 
in titrating standard acid in receiver flask 
after distillation of test sample; 

V3 = Volume, in ml, of standard acid taken in 
receiver flask for blank; 

V4 = Volume, in ml, of standard NaOH used 
in titrating standard acid in receiver flask 
after distillation in blank; 

N1 = Normality of standard acid; 

N2 = Normality of standard NaOH; 


W= Mass, in g, of sample taken; and 
df = Dilution factor of sample. 


IS 18146 : 2023 


ANNEX H 
[Table 1, 81 No. (ix)] 


ESTIMATION OF ARSENIC 


H-1 APPARATUS 


Analytical balance, beaker, hot plate, Whatman no. 1 
filter paper, volumetric flask (100 ml), atomic 
absorption spectrophotometer attached with vapour 
generation assembly. 


H-2 REAGENTS 


Aquaregia (HNO, + НСІ in a ratio of 1 : 3), 
concentrated hydrochloric acid, double distilled 
water, potassium iodide, standard arsenic solution. 


H-3 PROCEDURE 
H-3.1 Processing of Sample 


Suspend 10 g finely ground sample in 30 ml 
aquaregia (HNO, + НСІ in a ratio of 1 : 3) ina 
beaker. Keep on hot plate till moist black residue is 
obtained (do not dry). Add 5 ml aquaregia and allow 
to dry on hot plate till residue is moist. Dissolve the 
residue in 30 ml concentrated НСІ and filter through 


Whatman no.1 filter paper in 100 ml volumetric 
flask. Wash filter paper 3 - 4 times with double 
distilled water. Make up the volume to 100 ml. Take 
1 ml of this solution in 100 ml volumetric flask, add 
Sml concentrated hydrochloric acid and 2 g 
potassium iodide and make up the volume to 100 ml. 
Prepare standards having concentrations of 0.05 
ppm, 0.1 ppm and 0.2 ppm by diluting 0.05 ml, 
0.1 ml and 0.2 ml of standard arsenic solution with 
double distilled water in a volumetric flask by 
making up the volume to 100 ml. 


H-3.2 Measurement 


Estimate arsenic using vapour generation assembly 
attached to atomic absorption spectrophotometer as 
per the method given for instrument. 


H-3.3 Expression of Result 


Express the metal concentration as mg/kg on oven 
dry mass basis. 


ANNEX J 
[Table 1, 81 No. (х) to (xv)] 


ESTIMATION OF CADMIUM, COPPER, CHROMIUM, LEAD, NICKEL AND ZINC 


J-1 REAGENTS 
J-1.1 Diacid Mixture 


Mix 9 parts of nitric acid (HNO) and 4 parts of 
perchloric acid (HCIO,). 


J-1.2 Triacid Mixture 


Mix 10 parts of nitric acid (HNO,), 1 part of 
sulphuric acid (H, SO,) and 4 parts of Perchloric 
acid (HCIO,). 


J-1.3 Standard Cadmium Solution 
J-1.4 Standard Copper Solution 
J-1.5 Standard Chromium Solution 
J-1.6 Standard Lead Solution 

J-1.7 Standard Nickel Solution 


J-1.8 Standard Zinc Solution 


J-1.9 Double Distilled Water 


J-2 APPARATUS 


Analytical balance, hot air oven, 0.2 mm sieve, 
conical flask (250 ml), glass funnel, hot plate, 
Whatman filter paper no. 42, atomic absorption 
spectrophotometer, volumetric flasks (100 ml) 


J-3 PROCEDURE 
J-3.1 Processing of Sample 


Take 1.0 g or suitable quantity of oven dried (70 *C 
for 24 hours) sample thoroughly ground and sieved 
through 0.2 mm sieve in a conical flask. Add 30 ml 
triacid mixture (use diacid mixture for lead 
determination), cover it up with a small glass 
funnel for refluxing. Digest the sample at 
200 °C on a hot plat till the volume is 
significantly reduced with a whitish residue. After 
cooling, filter the sample through Whatman no. 42 
filter paper. Make up the volume to 100 ml with 
double distilled water in a volumetric flask. 


J-3.2 Preparation of Working Standards 


Dilute 1, 2, 3 and 4 ml of standard 100 ppm 
cadmium, copper, chromium, lead, nickel and zinc 
standard solution with double distilled water in 
separate volumetric flasks and makeup the volumes 
to 100 ml to obtain standards having concentrations 
of 1, 2, 3 and 4 ppm. 


J-3.3 Measurement 


Estimate the metal concentrations of cadmium, 


IS 18146 : 2023 


copper, chromium, lead, nickel and zinc by flaming 
the standardsand samples using atomic absorption 
spectrophotometer (AAS) as per the method given 
for instrument at recommended wavelength for each 
element. Run a blank following the same procedure. 


J-3.4 Expression of Result 


Express the metal concentration as mg/kg on dry 
mass basis. 


ANNEX K 
[Table 1, SI No. (xvi)] 


ESTIMATION OF MERCURY 


K-1 REAGENTS 
K-1.1 Concentrated Nitric Acid (HNO; ) 
K-1.2 Concentrated Sulphuric Acid (H:SO,) 


K-1.3 Potassium Persulphate 
Solution) 


(5 percent 


Dissolve 50g of K,S;0O; in 1 litre of distilled water. 


K-1.4 Potassium Permanganate (5 percent 
Solution) 


Dissolve 50 g of KMnO, in 1 litre of distilled water. 


K-1.5 
Solution 


Hydroxylamine Sodium Chloride 


Dissolve 120 g of Hydroxylamine salt and 120 g 
of sodium chloride (NaCl) in 1 litre of distilled 
water. 


K-1.6 Stannous Chloride (20 percent) 
Dissolve 20 g of SnCl, in 100 ml distilled water. 


K-1.7 Standard Mercury Solution 
K-1.8 Double Distilled Water 
K-2 APPARATUS 


Water bath, flameless atomic absorption 
spectrophotometer (AAS attached with vapour 
generation assembly that is, cold vapour mercury 
analyzer), BOD bottle (300 ml), analytical balance, 
hot air oven, volumetric flask (100 ml). 


K-3 PROCEDURE 
K-3.1 Processing of Sample 


Take 5 g (finely ground but not dried) sample in 
oven at temperature of 70 °C for 24 hour for 
moisture estimation. Take another 5 g sample 
(finely ground but not dried) in a BOD bottle, add 
to it 2.5 ml of concentrated HNO;, 5 ml of 
concentrated H,SO, and 15 ml of 5 percent 
KMnO4. After 15 min add 8 ml of 5 percent 
K,S,Os. Close the bottle with the lid and digest it 
on the water bath at 95 °C for 2 hour. After cooling 
to room temperature add 5 ml hydroxylamine 
sodium chloride solution. 


K-3.2 Preparation of Standard 


Prepare standards having concentrations of 
0.05 ppm, 0.1 ppm and 0.2 ppm by diluting 
0.05 ml, 0.1 ml and 0.2 ml of standardarsenic 
solution with double distilled water in a volumetric 
flask and make up the volume to 100 ml. 


K-3.3 Measurement 


Reduction of digested sample is brought out with 
5 ml of 20 percent SnCl, immediately before taking 
the readings. Estimate mercury concentration using 
a cold vapour mercury analyzer or atomic aborption 
spectrophotometry as per the method given for 
instrument. run a blank following the same 
procedure. 


K-3.4 Expression of Results 


Express the mercury concentration as mg/ kg on 
oven dry mass basis. 


IS 18146 : 2023

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication 8 Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: FAD 07 (16488).
